official_sources.title: NumPy argmin
official_sources.finding: argmin returns the index of the first occurrence when the minimum value occurs multiple times; with axis=None it operates on the flattened array.

official_sources.title: NumPy argmax
official_sources.finding: argmax returns the index of the first occurrence when the maximum occurs multiple times, so source traversal order cannot be allowed to define a terminal extrema cell.

official_sources.title: NumPy nanargmin
official_sources.finding: nanargmin ignores NaNs, raises ValueError for all-NaN slices, and warns results cannot be trusted for slices containing only NaNs and positive infinities.

official_sources.title: NumPy nanargmax
official_sources.finding: nanargmax ignores NaNs, raises ValueError for all-NaN slices, and warns results cannot be trusted for slices containing only NaNs and negative infinities.

official_sources.title: NumPy nanmin
official_sources.finding: nanmin ignores NaNs but still treats negative infinity as an extrema candidate; all-NaN slices emit a warning and return NaN.

official_sources.title: NumPy nanmax
official_sources.finding: nanmax ignores NaNs but still treats positive infinity as an extrema candidate; all-NaN slices emit a warning and return NaN.

official_sources.title: NumPy fmin
official_sources.finding: fmin has different NaN semantics from minimum: where possible it returns the non-NaN operand, demonstrating that NaN policy must be pinned rather than inferred from a generic minimum name.

official_sources.title: NumPy sort stability
official_sources.finding: sort is not stable by default; stable=True preserves the relative order of values that compare equal, and NaNs have an explicit extended sort order.

official_sources.title: NumPy argsort stability
official_sources.finding: argsort exposes stable sorting explicitly; without stable=True equal-key order is not guaranteed.

official_sources.title: NumPy lexsort
official_sources.finding: lexsort performs an indirect stable sort over multiple keys and defines which key is primary and how ties are broken, suitable for explicit value-row-column ordering.

official_sources.title: NumPy argpartition
official_sources.finding: argpartition documents that order within partitions is undefined, so it cannot be used to choose a deterministic terminal tie representative.

official_sources.title: NumPy ravel index order
official_sources.finding: ravel defines C/F/A/K index-order choices; default C order changes the last axis fastest, so flattening order is an explicit extrema-index dependency.

official_sources.title: NumPy ndarray.flatten
official_sources.finding: flatten defaults to C row-major order but can use F/A/K orders, meaning a first-occurrence extrema index can change if order is not pinned.

official_sources.title: NumPy unravel_index
official_sources.finding: unravel_index converts flat indices back to coordinates and explicitly takes C or Fortran order; the order must match the flattening convention.

official_sources.title: NumPy signbit
official_sources.finding: signbit exposes the floating-point sign bit as a boolean, allowing bit-sign provenance to be recorded separately from numeric equality where exact replay requires it.

official_sources.title: NumPy array_equal
official_sources.finding: array_equal requires equal shapes and equal elements, making it appropriate for exact tie-set bitmap or cell-id replay rather than tolerance-based equivalence.

official_sources.title: NumPy allclose
official_sources.finding: allclose uses rtol/atol and can accept unequal values; its default atol is explicitly warned as inappropriate for some magnitudes, so it is QA-only for terminal extrema identity.

official_sources.title: NumPy where
official_sources.finding: where selects values under an explicit boolean condition; extrema tie-set construction can therefore be based on an exact equality mask after validity filtering rather than a traversal-dependent arg index.

official_sources.title: GDALRasterBand block and RasterIO semantics
official_sources.finding: GDAL exposes natural block size, actual edge-block size, ReadBlock without resampling/type conversion, and RasterIO which may resample or translate datatype; edge-block bytes beyond valid raster extent are undetermined.

official_sources.title: GDAL multi-threading guidance
official_sources.finding: GDAL warns ordinary dataset/raster-band instances are stateful and not safe for concurrent calls; read-only thread-safe dataset support exists from GDAL 3.10 with distinct per-thread handling.

official_sources.title: gdalinfo exact and approximate statistics
official_sources.finding: gdalinfo -mm forces actual min/max while approximate statistics may use overviews or a subset of tiles, so approximate statistics are not terminal extrema evidence.

official_sources.title: gdal raster info min-max and statistics
official_sources.finding: gdal raster info can force actual min/max and all-pixel statistics, providing an independent full-raster QA channel distinct from stored or approximate statistics.
